🇨🇳 🇺🇸 China cuts US Treasury holdings to an 18-year low • China has been reducing its holdings for over a decade, down from around $1.3 trillion in the early 2010s to $618 billion today. • The decline accelerated after 2022 as China became more concerned about relying too heavily on US assets. • Foreign governments are buying fewer US Treasuries, while hedge funds and other investors are buying more. • Weaker foreign demand is helping push Treasury yields higher, with the 30-year yield recently hitting a nearly 20-year high. • Higher yields mean the US government has to pay more to borrow money. @WatcherGuru

Goldman Sachs, Citizens: SEC Innovation Exemption Framework Could Benefit Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle Goldman Sachs and Citizens analysts said the SEC’s five-year “innovation exemption” framework could benefit Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle by allowing qualifying tokenized U.S. stocks to trade through AMMs on public blockchains. Coinbase could benefit from custody, tokenization infrastructure, stablecoins and Base; Robinhood would need to add full shareholder rights to its offshore stock-token products; Circle could benefit from greater demand for USDC settlement and collateral. Trading limits, issuer opt-out rights and AMM constraints could limit the impact on traditional exchanges. — link

Highlight Clip: Circle CPTO: Arc Won't Grow by Simply Moving Ethereum's Business Circle CPTO: Arc Won't Grow by Simply Moving Ethereum's Business Circle Chief Product and Technology Officer Nikhil Chandhok said in a September 16 interview with Bankless that Ethereum is the largest blockchain for USDC. Simply moving existing activity and USDC from Ethereum to Arc would not expand the overall market. Chandhok believes AI agents will become independent economic actors that need to prove what work they have performed online. He wants Arc to enable agents to record their activities and use cryptographic proofs to verify their work history and actual economic output, creating new on-chain demand. — link

Uniswap Founder: SBF Once Bought the Uniswap[.]com Domain for Seven Figures, Later Acquired for Free by Its Legal Team Uniswap founder Hayden Adams said that the previous owner of the Uniswap[.]com domain had asked for a seven-figure sum, but his team refused to pay. SBF later purchased the domain for seven figures and redirected it to a forked project. Due to the domain’s malicious use, his legal team ultimately obtained it for free. — link
